note: Nine curated overall-change reactions. Equations and atom pairing are checked by scripts/validate-organic.cjs. Animations are not mechanisms.
mechanismNote: This animation shows the overall change, not the detailed mechanism.

reactions.name: Combustion of methane
reactions.conditions: Air or oxygen; a flame or spark to start
reactions.safety: Flammable gas. Use only as a teacher demonstration with correct ventilation.
reactions.explanation: Methane burns in oxygen to form carbon dioxide and water. Complete combustion needs a good supply of oxygen.
reactions.mechanismNote: This animation shows the overall change, not the detailed mechanism.

steps.title: Reactants
steps.text: One methane molecule and two oxygen molecules are ready to react.

steps.title: Contact
steps.text: In a flame the molecules collide with enough energy for bonds to rearrange.

steps.title: Products
steps.text: Carbon dioxide and two water molecules form. Heat and light are released.

reactions.name: Substitution: methane and chlorine
reactions.safety: Chlorine is toxic. This is a classroom model only.
reactions.explanation: In ultraviolet light, a hydrogen atom in methane is replaced by a chlorine atom. Chloromethane and hydrogen chloride form.
reactions.mechanismNote: This animation shows the overall change, not the detailed mechanism.

steps.title: Reactants
steps.text: Methane and chlorine are shown before the reaction.

steps.title: Under UV light
steps.text: Ultraviolet light supplies the energy that starts the substitution.

steps.title: Products
steps.text: Chloromethane and hydrogen chloride are the overall products.

reactions.name: Addition of bromine to ethene
reactions.safety: Bromine is corrosive and toxic. Use bromine water only under teacher supervision.
reactions.explanation: Bromine adds across the C=C bond of ethene. The orange colour of bromine disappears as 1,2-dibromoethane forms.
reactions.mechanismNote: This animation shows the overall change, not the detailed mechanism.

steps.title: Reactants
steps.text: Ethene has a double bond. Bromine is the orange-brown halogen.

steps.title: Contact
steps.text: The bromine molecule approaches the double bond.

steps.title: Product
steps.text: Both bromine atoms join the carbon chain. The double bond becomes a single bond.

reactions.name: Hydrogenation of ethene
reactions.conditions: Hydrogen gas with a nickel catalyst, heat
reactions.explanation: Hydrogen adds across the double bond of ethene to give ethane. A nickel catalyst is used in the school-level description.
reactions.mechanismNote: This animation shows the overall change, not the detailed mechanism.

steps.title: Reactants
steps.text: Ethene and hydrogen are the starting materials.

steps.title: On the catalyst
steps.text: On a nickel surface the molecules can join more easily.

steps.title: Product
steps.text: Ethane forms. The C=C bond has become a C–C bond.

reactions.name: Halogenation: ethene and hydrogen bromide
reactions.safety: Hydrogen bromide is corrosive. Classroom model only.
reactions.explanation: Hydrogen bromide adds across the double bond of ethene to give bromoethane.
reactions.mechanismNote: This animation shows the overall change, not the detailed mechanism.

steps.title: Reactants
steps.text: Ethene and hydrogen bromide are shown separately.

steps.title: Contact
steps.text: HBr approaches the double bond.

steps.title: Product
steps.text: Bromoethane forms as H and Br add to the two carbons.

reactions.name: Hydration of ethene
reactions.conditions: Steam with an acid catalyst, heat and pressure
reactions.safety: Industrial conditions are hot and pressurised. Classroom model only.
reactions.explanation: Steam adds across the double bond of ethene to give ethanol. This is an important industrial route to ethanol.
reactions.mechanismNote: This animation shows the overall change, not the detailed mechanism.

steps.title: Reactants
steps.text: Ethene and water (as steam) are the reactants.

steps.title: Contact
steps.text: Under catalytic conditions water adds to the double bond.

steps.title: Product
steps.text: Ethanol forms. An –OH group is now present.

reactions.name: Dehydration of ethanol
reactions.safety: Concentrated acids are corrosive. Teacher demonstration only.
reactions.explanation: Water is removed from ethanol and ethene forms. Dehydration is the reverse of hydration in overall terms.
reactions.mechanismNote: This animation shows the overall change, not the detailed mechanism.

steps.title: Reactant
steps.text: Ethanol contains an –OH group.

steps.title: Heating with catalyst
steps.text: Strong heating with an acid catalyst drives water out.

steps.title: Products
steps.text: Ethene and water are produced.

reactions.name: Polymerization of ethene
reactions.conditions: High pressure and a catalyst (industrial overview)
reactions.safety: Industrial process. This Lab shows a short model segment only.
reactions.explanation: Many ethene molecules join to make poly(ethene). Here three ethene units form a short open-chain segment to show the idea.
reactions.mechanismNote: This animation shows the overall change, not the detailed mechanism.

steps.title: Monomers
steps.text: Three ethene monomers are shown.

steps.title: Joining
steps.text: The double bonds open so the carbons can link into a chain.

steps.title: Polymer segment
steps.text: A short poly(ethene) segment forms. Real chains are much longer.

reactions.name: Esterification
reactions.safety: Handle acids carefully. Classroom model of the organic change.
reactions.explanation: Ethanoic acid reacts with methanol to form methyl ethanoate and water. Esters often have fruity smells.
reactions.mechanismNote: This animation shows the overall change, not the detailed mechanism.

steps.title: Reactants
steps.text: A carboxylic acid and an alcohol are the starting materials.

steps.title: Contact
steps.text: With an acid catalyst the molecules combine and water is released.

steps.title: Products
steps.text: Methyl ethanoate and water are the overall products.
